## Follow changes

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://huggingface.co/api/buckets/string/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/buckets/{namespace}/{repo}/events`

Server-sent events (`Accept: text/event-stream`) of the bucket's file changes, so clients can stop polling `/tree`.

Events:
- `ready`: `{"cursor"}` — replay (if any) is done, live changes follow. `cursor` may be absent if the feed has seen no change yet.
- `changes`: `{"cursor", "changes": [{"path", "op": "add" | "update" | "delete", "size"?, "xetHash"?, "uploadedAt"?, "mtime"?, "mtimeNanos"?}]}` — a batch of changes coalesced over ~200ms. An `update` only carries the fields that changed (an identical re-upload has just `uploadedAt`); `mtime`/`mtimeNanos` are `null` when a re-upload cleared them. `xetHash` is omitted without content read access.
- `reset`: `{"reason": "cursor_too_old"}` — the requested `cursor`/`since` is older than what the server buffers (about 15 minutes); the stream ends and the client must re-list. A `since` at or after the bucket's `updatedAt` never resets, however old.
- `reconnect`: `{"cursor"}` — sent after 20 minutes or when the server shuts down (deploys), then the stream ends; reconnect with that cursor. Treat any other end of the stream the same way: reconnect with the last cursor you received.

A `: ping` comment is sent every 30s. Resume with `?cursor=` (exclusive) or `?since=` (inclusive); without either, only live changes are sent.

<h3 id="follow-changes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|repo|path|string|true|none|
|cursor|query|string|false|none|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="follow-changes-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|503|Service Unavailable|Live follow is not served by this instance, or not caught up yet; retry after `Retry-After` seconds|Inline|

<h3 id="follow-changes-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **503**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|true|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="hub-api-endpoints-containers">containers</h1>

Container image repositories, usable with the Hugging Face container registry (`docker push` / `docker pull`). Backed by bucket storage: the file endpoints mirror the bucket ones. Also includes the registry token endpoint used by `docker login`.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

|uploadedAt|string|true|none|ISO 8601 timestamp of when the file was added to the bucket|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|true|none|none|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Batch file operations

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://huggingface.co/api/containers/string/string/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/containers/{namespace}/{repo}/batch`

Accepts NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) where each line is an addFile, copyFile, or deleteFile instruction.
All add/copy operations must come before all delete operations.

JSON-lines payload:
```json
	'{"type":"addFile","path":"...","xetHash":"...","mtime":...,"mtimeNanos":...,"contentType":"..."}' +
	'{"type":"copyFile","path":"...","xetHash":"...","sourceRepoType":"...","sourceRepoId":"...","mtime":...,"mtimeNanos":...,"contentType":"..."}' +
	'{"type":"deleteFile","path":"..."}'
```

<h3 id="batch-file-operations-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|repo|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "processed": -9007199254740000,
  "succeeded": -9007199254740000,
  "failed": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "error": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "processed": -9007199254740000,
  "succeeded": -9007199254740000,
  "failed": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "error": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="batch-file-operations-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Batch operation status|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Batch operation status|Inline|

<h3 id="batch-file-operations-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|success|boolean|true|none|True if all operations succeeded|
|processed|integer|true|none|Total number of operations attempted|
|succeeded|integer|true|none|Number of successful operations|
|failed|[object]|true|none|List of failed operations|
|» path|string|true|none|File path that failed|
|» error|string|true|none|Error message|

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|success|boolean|true|none|True if all operations succeeded|
|processed|integer|true|none|Total number of operations attempted|
|succeeded|integer|true|none|Number of successful operations|
|failed|[object]|true|none|List of failed operations|
|» path|string|true|none|File path that failed|
|» error|string|true|none|Error message|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/inference-endpoints/{namespace}/auth-check/{perms}`

Check if the user has access to the inference endpoint

<h3 id="check-access-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|perms|path|string|true|none|
|own|query|string|false|none|
|is_creator|query|string|false|none|
|creator_id|query|string|false|none|
|incur_cost|query|string|false|none|
|resource_group_id|query|string|false|none|
|repo_id|query|string|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|perms|write|
|perms|infer|

> 200 Response

```json

  "namespace": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "hasHfLevelAccess": true
  },
  "resourceGroupId": "string"
}
```

> 207 Response

```json
{
  "namespace": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "hasHfLevelAccess": true
  },

    "string"
  ],

}
```

```bash
  -d '{

      "http://example.com"
    ],
    "client_name": "string",
    "client_uri": "http://example.com",
    "logo_uri": "http://example.com",
    "scope": "string",
    "contacts": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "client_secret_basic",
    "software_id": "string",
    "software_version": "string"
  }'
```

<h1 id="hub-api-endpoints-scim">scim</h1>

Use the SCIM API to control and manage your hub Enterprise organization manage members' access.
## Authentication

- Must be organization owner
- Use Access token with write permission on organization
- Organization must be Enterprise Plus

## Key Attribute Matching

- Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)
	* SAML: `http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/objectidentifier`
	* SCIM: `externalId`
- Other Identity Providers
	* SAML: `NameID` or `unique identifier`
	* SCIM: `externalId`

## Supported SCIM User Attributes

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| `userName` | Username for the user |
| `name.givenName` | First name |
| `name.familyName` | Last name |
| `emails` | Array of user emails; we don't support email types |
| `externalId` | IDP provider's unique identifier |
| `id` | Hugging Face SCIM endpoint identifier |
| `active` | Boolean for provisioning status |

## Create SCIM user

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://huggingface.co/api/organizations/string/scim/v2/Users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "schemas": [
      "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
    ],
    "userName": "string",
    "emails": [
      {
        "value": "user@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "name": {
      "givenName": "string",
      "familyName": "string"
    },
    "active": true,
    "externalId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/organizations/{name}/scim/v2/Users`

Creates a new user in the organization. If the user already exists, only `active` field will be updated to provision the user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "userName": "string",
  "emails": [
    {
      "value": "user@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "name": {
    "givenName": "string",
    "familyName": "string"
  },
  "active": true,
  "externalId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-scim-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» schemas|body|[string]|true|none|
|» userName|body|string|true|Username for the user, it should respect the hub rules: No consecutive dashes, No digit-only, Does not start or end with a dash, Only dashes, letters or numbers, Not 24 chars hex string|
|» emails|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » value|body|string(email)|true|none|
|» name|body|object|true|none|
|» » givenName|body|string|true|none|
|» » familyName|body|string|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» externalId|body|string|true|External ID for the user, it must be unique within the organization and is required for managed users|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "id": "123",
  "externalId": "unique-identifier",
  "userName": "username",
  "displayName": "username (equals to userName)",
  "name": {
    "givenName": "John",
    "familyName": "Doe",
    "formatted": "John Doe"
  },
  "emails": [
    {
      "value": "john.doe@example.com",
      "primary": true,
      "type": "work"
    }
  ],
  "active": true,
  "meta": {
    "resourceType": "User",
    "location": "https://huggingface.co/api/organizations/:name/scim/v2/Users/:id"
  }
}
```

```bash
  }'
```

`PUT /api/organizations/{name}/scim/v2/Users/{userId}`

Updates a provisioned user, you'll need to provide all their information fresh - just like setting them up for the first time. Any details you don't include will be automatically removed, so make sure to include everything they need to keep their account running smoothly. Setting `active` to `false` will deprovision the user from the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "userName": "string",
  "emails": [
    {
      "value": "user@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "name": {
    "givenName": "string",
    "familyName": "string"
  },
  "active": true,
  "externalId": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|userId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» schemas|body|[string]|true|none|
|» userName|body|string|true|Username for the user, it should respect the hub rules: No consecutive dashes, No digit-only, Does not start or end with a dash, Only dashes, letters or numbers, Not 24 chars hex string|
|» emails|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » value|body|string(email)|true|none|
|» name|body|object|true|none|
|» » givenName|body|string|true|none|
|» » familyName|body|string|true|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» externalId|body|string|true|none|

`PATCH /api/organizations/{name}/scim/v2/Users/{userId}`

Update an attribute of a SCIM user. Modify individual attributes using Operations format. Just provide the changes you want to make using add, remove (only `externalId` is supported), or replace operations.
 If you set `active` to `false`, the user will be deprovisioned from the organization.

`GET /api/agent-harnesses`

Get the registry of AI agents / harnesses known to the Hub, along with the standard environment variables used to detect them. Clients use this registry to identify which agent they are running in when reporting Hub activity.

```json
      }
```

|» » description|string|false|none|Short description of the harness|

<h1 id="hub-api-endpoints-tokens">tokens</h1>

## Revoke leaked tokens

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://huggingface.co/api/credentials/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "credentials": [
      "hf_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/credentials/revoke`

Publicly invalidate leaked Hugging Face access tokens. Possession of the raw token value is the only proof required: no authentication is needed, and no rights over the owning account or org are necessary. Each raw token is fully invalidated, the owning user is notified by email. Always returns 202, whether or not any of the provided tokens existed, so the response cannot be used to probe token validity.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    "hf_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-leaked-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» credentials|body|[string]|true|Raw access token values to invalidate, at most 1000.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>
